title: Microsoft SSO integration on macOS fails for SAML use cases
body: I am using Firefox 133 on macOS with a Company Portal-managed device that is marked compliant. I enabled network.http.microsoft-entra-sso.enabled, but Entra ID SAML applications show a Microsoft login prompt and, after credentials and MFA, reject access because the device is reported as unregistered with no device identifier. On the same machine, OpenID Connect applications successfully use Company Portal SSO and receive the managed and compliant device state. Both a public SAML application and an internal SAML application fail. Manually adding autologon.microsoftazuread-sso.com and device.login.microsoftonline.com to network.microsoft-sso-authority-list does not change the failures.

symptoms_visible: When I open an Entra ID SAML application, I get a Microsoft login prompt and then, after credentials and MFA, a message saying I cannot access the resource.
The sign-in details say 'Device state: Unregistered' and 'Device identifier: Not available', even though Company Portal reports this Mac as compliant.
On the same Mac, OpenID Connect applications use SSO successfully and show the device as managed and compliant.
Both my public Docker Hub SAML example and an internal SAML application fail in the same way.
N0.label: N0 SAML SSO failure reported

symptoms_visible: The SAML login still reports my device as unregistered.
My SAML recording contains no macOSSingleSignOn messages, while the OIDC recording invokes MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils and returns device credential headers.
N1.label: N1 contrasting HTTP logs collected

symptoms_visible: Both previously failing SAML applications work through SSO in the signed test build.
The test-build log invokes macOSSingleSignOn for the /tenant/saml2 URL and receives device credential headers.
OIDC still works in the test build.
N2.label: N2 candidate patch verified

symptoms_visible: The installed Firefox 133 build still fails for the SAML applications, while the signed test build authenticates both of them successfully.
N3.label: N3 URI restriction reviewed

symptoms_visible: After updating to Firefox 134, my previously affected SAML sites authenticate properly through Company Portal SSO.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved in Firefox 134

question_patterns: Can you record HTTP logs with nsHttp:5,macOSSingleSignOn:5 while attempting both the failing SAML login and a working OIDC login?
Please capture about:logging output for the SAML attempt and compare it with the OIDC flow.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I recorded both from a fresh Firefox profile. The SAML log has no mention of macOSSingleSignOn. In the OIDC log, I see MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils being created, AddMicrosoftEntraSSO starting for the /oauth2/v2.0/authorize URL, and didCompleteWithAuthorization returning an ASAuthorizationSingleSignOnCredential with x-ms-DeviceCredential headers.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both recordings invoke macOSSingleSignOn and return the same device credential headers, including the failing SAML attempt.
The same contrast appears in logs captured from my existing profile rather than a fresh profile.

edges.comment: The reporter privately supplied the requested logging evidence and publicly described its raw contents. Alongside the answer, the reporter noted that Entra SAML posts to https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT/saml2 without a query and independently suspected the query-emptiness condition in nsHttpChannel.

question_patterns: Can you test this signed build against the two SAML applications that currently fail and also check that OIDC still works?
Please try the provided candidate build and report what happens with the same SAML and OIDC sign-ins.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Tested. Both SAML2 applications that previously failed now work through SSO. The log now contains AddMicrosoftEntraSSO for https://login.microsoftonline.com/XXXXXXXX/saml2 and later shows didCompleteWithAuthorization with device credential headers. OIDC is still working; I did not spot a regression.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The signed build still prompts for credentials and reports the device as unregistered on both SAML applications.
Only one of my two SAML applications is available to test, but it works and OIDC remains working.

edges.comment: Pre-landing verification of a signed candidate build is a measurement. The reporter supplied only the observed application and log results; the definitive interpretation of the query guard remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Do you see any compatibility concerns with retaining a path-based exclusion while enabling SAML?
Can you review the revised path/query condition against the SAML endpoint and possible URI edge cases?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am concerned that a path-based replacement is still too restrictive. GetPathQueryRef appears to contain at least a leading slash, and requiring multiple slashes could break if Microsoft ever changes /TENANT/saml2 to /saml2. It also seems possible to satisfy slash-counting with odd root URLs or fragments. Why is the root-URI exclusion needed on macOS at all when the Windows path does not apply the same restriction?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I confirmed that every supported Entra SAML endpoint always has a tenant path with at least two slashes, so retaining that path restriction is safe.
The test build's application icon looks the same as my installed Firefox.

edges.comment: The reporter volunteered this technical review after the successful candidate test. It helped motivate removing the URI query/path gate entirely rather than replacing it with brittle slash counting.

solution.intent: Remove the macOS Entra SSO query-emptiness gate so document and subdocument requests to queryless SAML endpoints invoke the native SSO API, while retaining the existing authority and preference checks and allowing invalid root URLs to fall through after the API returns an error.
solution.concrete_example: Patch nsHttpChannel to stop requiring a non-empty URI query before calling MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils on macOS. This allows POST requests to https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT/saml2 to acquire the Company Portal device credentials. Bare or invalid authority URLs can return didCompleteWithError from the native API and then continue normally. Ask the reporter to retest the affected sites in a regular Firefox build containing the landed patch.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter exposed the raw contrast—no macOSSingleSignOn activity for the queryless SAML POST, normal SSO activity for OIDC—and proposed the relevant code condition. Engineers confirmed that the non-empty GetQuery check was the blocker, determined that the native API safely returns didCompleteWithError for unsuitable root URLs, and chose to remove the check as on Windows.

edges.comment: The patch removing the GetQuery check landed after the signed-build test. The reporter later confirmed the same previously affected sites worked in Firefox 134; that post-landing release verification is terminal-side and is not required evidence for proposing the patch.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: the macOS Entra SSO path in nsHttpChannel required a non-empty URI query, so queryless SAML POSTs to /TENANT/saml2 never invoked MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils and therefore did not receive Company Portal device credentials.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the contrasting SAML and OIDC logs and the successful signed test build, not inferred from the access-denied page alone.
The technical fix must remove the query-emptiness check for macOS Entra SSO so SAML endpoints can reach the native SSO API; invalid root URLs can safely fall through when that API returns an error.
Must not recommend adding Microsoft domains to network.microsoft-sso-authority-list as the resolution, because those additions were already tried without changing the failure.

Must ask the reporter to verify the affected SAML sites on a normal build containing the landed fix and must not declare resolution until that verification; the reporter confirmed success in Firefox 134.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical enterprise user: understands Entra ID, SAML, OIDC, MDM compliance, Firefox logging, and can inspect C++ networking conditions and review patch edge cases, but is not familiar with all Firefox internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, evidence-driven, and collaborative; supplies comparisons, redacted log excerpts, screenshots, and source links, tests signed builds promptly, and challenges brittle implementation assumptions with concrete URI examples.
